thesis: Sai in the command zone turns each of the deck's 43 artifact spells into a cast plus a 1/1 flying Thopter, so the board goes wide on its own; the game ends when an artifact-count scaler (Master of Etherium, Chief of the Foundry, Steel Overseer, Nettlecyst, Adaptive Omnitool — with Forsaken Monument's flat +2/+2 on the colourless ones) or a self-scaling body (Darksteel Juggernaut, Broodstar, Myr Battlesphere, Graaz, Kappa Cannoneer) turns that width into damage, while Sai's sacrifice-two-draw and the artifact draw suite keep the casts coming.

stages.label: FORTY LANDS AND NINE ARTIFACT ROCKS
stages.what_it_does: Forty lands (34 Island, Lonely Sandbar, Remote Isle, Darksteel Citadel, Buried Ruin, Foundry of the Consuls, War Room) and nine nonland producers (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Mind Stone, Thought Vessel, Hedron Archive, Palladium Myr, Silver Myr, Ornithopter of Paradise, Cultivator's Caravan). deck-facts: 36 blue land sources (mana_analysis counts 41 with the five nonland blue producers) against a blue pip load of 33 pips over 26 cards, no card asking more than two; deck-audit reads mana-base 40 copies OVER the 36-38 base target and ramp 18 copies OVER the 10-12 target. The goldfish reads mean available mana 3.439 on turn 3 and 6.778 on turn 6; the declared ACCELERANT group (eleven cards, this stage's nine plus the two cost reducers) is in 57.4% of openers and drawn by turn 6 in 82.5% of games, mean turn 2.534. Every one of the nine nonland producers is an artifact spell, so under Sai each one lands with a Thopter beside it: this stage is the first fodder as well as the mana. Nine of the forty-nine make only {C} (Sol Ring, Palladium Myr, Hedron Archive, Mind Stone, Thought Vessel, Citadel, Buried Ruin, Foundry, War Room), which pays for the colourless artifacts; Forsaken Monument adds one more {C} per tap of any of them — three from Sol Ring, Palladium Myr and Hedron Archive, two from the six one-{C} sources — because the 2020-09-25 ruling says a tap for more than one {C} still adds only one. Caravan needs crew 3 to attack and is counted here as a rock. Mind Stone and Hedron Archive sacrifice themselves to draw late; Buried Ruin returns an artifact; Foundry of the Consuls makes two Thopters for {5}; War Room draws for {3} and one life.

evidence.note: eleven of the sixteen sit together (Signet, Caravan, Citadel, Buried Ruin, Foundry, Archive, Mind Stone, Ornithopter, Sol Ring, Vessel, War Room); the Islands and the two cycling lands are in city-1, Palladium Myr in city-0, Silver Myr in city-3
seven rocks plus three ramp:dork — the role says what each is for, not that they interact

stages.label: SAI RESOLVES
stages.what_it_does: Sai, Master Thopterist is the first thing that has to happen: 'Whenever you cast an artifact spell, create a 1/1 colorless Thopter artifact creature token with flying.' Only two other cards in the 99 trigger on a cast at all — Vedalken Archmage draws on an artifact cast and Forsaken Monument gains 2 life on a colourless one — and neither makes a body, so until Sai is on the battlefield the deck is 43 artifact spells doing their own printed jobs. The goldfish casts him on mean turn 2.979 (median 3; 8,968 of 10,000 games on turn 3) and by turn 6 in 99.7% of games. From there every artifact cast is two artifacts on the board (the spell and the token), which is what the conversion stage counts and what the fodder stage feeds: his second ability, {1}{U} and sacrifice two artifacts, draws a card, so two Thopters are a card whenever the hand runs dry. The goldfish does NOT model either ability (goldfish_targets._model_note; model-coverage reads nothing dark because no corpus card shares the text), so every bodies and damage figure in this model is a floor that leaves out the Thopters. Sai is a creature, not an artifact: he dies to Nevinyrral's Disk and to All Is Dust, has no hexproof from Padeem, and the deck has no recursion that reaches the command zone, so each re-cast costs two more. The engine degrades rather than stops without him: 24 of the deck's creatures are artifact creatures, no scaler needs Thopters specifically (they count artifacts, artifact creatures or colourless creatures), and Thopter Spy Network and Thopter Fabricator make tokens on their own, so a Sai-less board still grows, just one body per cast instead of two.

evidence.note: checker-passed: Sai's trigger resolves before the artifact spell that caused it (601.2i, 603.3, 405.5); the Thopter is on the battlefield before Chief of the Foundry is
Sai clusters with Master of Etherium, Etherium Sculptor, Whirler Rogue and the affinity cantrips — the map sees 'artifact' in the text, not that he is the one that starts it
the role tags the token making; it does not say the tokens are what every other stage runs on

stages.label: ARTIFACTS INTO HAND, AND CHEAPER
stages.what_it_does: What keeps the casts coming once Sai is out: the draw that refills the hand with artifacts and the two discounts that let two or three land in one turn. Etherium Sculptor and Foundry Inspector each make artifact spells cost {1} less; with both out, the deck's 25 nonland artifacts under mana value 4 mostly cost one or nothing. Vedalken Archmage draws a card on the same trigger Sai makes a Thopter on, so every artifact cast is a body AND a card. Thought Monitor, Thoughtcast (affinity) and Thirst for Knowledge (discard an artifact instead of two cards) are the burst draw; Pull from Tomorrow is the late refill; Mazemind Tome, Tamiyo's Logbook (cheaper per other artifact) and Mind's Eye are the mana-sink engines; Research Thief draws when an artifact creature connects. The goldfish reads the declared DRAW group (nineteen cards: nine of this stage's — Archmage, Thief, Monitor, Thoughtcast, Thirst, Pull, Tome, Logbook, Eye — plus Wellspring, both Crawlers, Spy Network, Fabricator, Shimmer Dragon, Spellbomb, Archive, Mind Stone and Lantern) in 78.7% of openers and drawn by turn 6 in 95.1% of games, mean turn 1.544, and mean extra cards drawn 1.328 by turn 6 and 4.967 by turn 10 — a floor, because goldfish_metrics.meta.card_advantage.draw_not_modelled names seven of the nineteen (Tome, Eye, Psychosis Crawler, Thief, Spy Network, Thoughtcast, Shimmer Dragon) as contributing nothing to it. The ACCELERANT group's 82.5% by turn 6 includes the two reducers. Archmage, Thoughtcast, Thirst and Pull are not artifacts and do not trigger Sai; the other seven here (Sculptor, Inspector, Thief, Monitor, Tome, Logbook, Eye) are artifact spells and do. The deck has zero tutors (bracket_report), so the fuel is draw or nothing.

evidence.note: Archmage, Monitor, Thoughtcast, Thirst and Sculptor sit in city-3; Thief, Pull and the Logbook in city-1; the Tome, the Eye and Inspector in city-0
eight cards carry it; five are in this stage (Sculptor, Inspector, Monitor, Thoughtcast, Logbook) and three are placed elsewhere (Broodstar in wincon, Memory Guardian and Spire Golem in output)

stages.label: THE BODIES SAI EATS
stages.what_it_does: The deck converts artifacts on the board into cards and into evasion: Sai's {1}{U} sacrifice two artifacts draws a card, Shimmer Dragon taps two untapped artifacts to draw, Whirler Rogue taps two to make a creature unblockable, Kappa Cannoneer taps them to improvise its cost, and the Vehicles crew with them. The resource eaten is mostly Thopter tokens, which are not cards and which the goldfish never creates. The four cards here are the ones whose job is to supply or to be that resource: Thopter Spy Network makes a Thopter at every upkeep with no cast at all, and draws when artifact creatures connect; Thopter Fabricator makes one whenever a second card is drawn in a turn (Archmage, Monitor, Thirst and Sai's own draw all reach that); Ichor Wellspring draws when it enters and again when it is sacrificed, so feeding it to Sai is two cards for {1}{U}; Myr Retriever returns another artifact card from the graveyard when it dies, so sacrificing it to Sai gets a spent Wellspring, Spellbomb or Mind Stone back to be cast again — and cast again means another Thopter. The goldfish reads mean bodies 2.567 by turn 6 and 6.729 by turn 10 with none of this modelled, which is why it is a floor and why this is the stage the map cannot see at all: nothing in these four texts says 'sacrifice'.

evidence.note: Wellspring and Retriever in city-0, Spy Network in city-1, Fabricator in city-4 — four cards, three cities

stages.label: COUNT THE ARTIFACTS
stages.what_it_does: The engine proper: what turns a wide artifact board into power or into cards. Master of Etherium has power equal to artifacts you control and gives other artifact creatures +1/+1; Chief of the Foundry gives them +1/+1; Steel Overseer taps to put a +1/+1 counter on every artifact creature, Thopters included; Nettlecyst and Adaptive Omnitool make one creature +1/+1 per artifact (Omnitool also digs an artifact when it attacks); Forsaken Monument gives colourless creatures +2/+2 — every Thopter and Myr token and 17 of the deck's 24 artifact creatures, but not the seven blue ones (Sculptor, Master of Etherium, Kappa, Transmuter, Memory Guardian, Research Thief, Thought Monitor) — and adds one more {C} each time a permanent is tapped for {C}. Whirler Rogue brings two Thopters and taps two artifacts to make a creature unblockable, so the board becomes one connecting body; Shimmer Dragon taps two artifacts to draw and is hexproof at four artifacts; Master Transmuter bounces an artifact (a token will do) to put an artifact from hand onto the battlefield, which is how a seven- or eight-mana body arrives for {U} — but putting onto the battlefield is not casting, so Sai makes no Thopter for it. The goldfish reads the declared PAYOFF group (Chief, Master, Nettlecyst, Overseer, Omnitool, Monument, Padeem, Spy Network, Archmage) in 49.8% of openers and by turn 6 in 77.0% of games, mean turn 2.79; mean board power 4.939 by turn 6 and 13.704 by turn 10, with zero Thopters counted. Every card here except Rogue and the Dragon is itself an artifact spell. The three scalers phrase the same job three ways, and the map splits them across three cities on that phrasing.

evidence.note: Master of Etherium, Rogue and Transmuter in city-3; Chief, Overseer and Monument in city-0; Nettlecyst, Omnitool and the Dragon in city-4
four cards carry it; the role does not say what they count

stages.label: REMOVAL, DRAIN AND THE FLYERS
stages.what_it_does: What the engine produces short of the kill. Removal: Duplicant exiles a nontoken creature on entry, Meteor Golem destroys a nonland permanent, Skysovereign deals 3 to a creature or planeswalker on entry and on each attack, Aether Spellbomb bounces a creature for {U} or draws for {1}, Fall from Favor taps a creature down and makes you the monarch (a draw a turn while it holds). The two resets: Nevinyrral's Disk destroys all artifacts, creatures and enchantments — Darksteel Juggernaut and Darksteel Citadel survive it, Sai does not; All Is Dust makes each player sacrifice coloured permanents, which in this deck is 19 nonland permanents including Sai, Master of Etherium, Etherium Sculptor, Kappa Cannoneer and Master Transmuter, while every colourless artifact creature and every Thopter stays. Soul-Guide Lantern exiles a graveyard and cycles itself. Drain: Psychosis Crawler makes each opponent lose 1 per card you draw and Scrawling Crawler 1 per card they draw — the goldfish reads cumulative event damage 2.92 by turn 10, so this is incidental, not a clock. Flyers: Memory Guardian and Spire Golem are affinity 3/4 and 2/4 flyers that cost little on a wide board and carry the anthems over blockers. The declared ANSWER group (twelve cards: seven of this stage's — Duplicant, Meteor Golem, Skysovereign, Spellbomb, Fall from Favor, the Disk, All Is Dust — plus Counterspell, Negate, Launch Mishap and Aetherize from protection and Steel Hellkite from wincon) is in 60.7% of openers and drawn by turn 6 in 85.4% of games; deck-audit counts interaction 9 against a target of 8, with four classes answered against five and no answer to a land.

evidence.note: Duplicant, Golem, Disk, All Is Dust, Lantern and both Crawlers in city-0; Skysovereign in city-4; Spellbomb and Fall from Favor in city-1; Guardian and Spire Golem in city-3

stages.label: COUNTERS, FOG AND HEXPROOF
stages.what_it_does: What keeps the board alive. Counterspell, Negate and Launch Mishap (which also makes a Thopter) are the three counters; Aetherize bounces every attacker; Propaganda taxes each attacker {2}; Misleading Signpost flashes in during declare attackers to point an attacker elsewhere and then taps for {U}. Padeem gives every artifact hexproof and draws each upkeep if you hold the biggest artifact — Sai himself is not an artifact and gets none of it. Shimmer Myr lets artifact spells be cast as though they had flash, which is the deck's answer to a sorcery-speed wrath: hold the artifacts, cast them on the end step, and Sai's Thopters arrive with counter mana still up. deck-audit reads protection 4 copies UNDER the 5-7 base target and notes Darksteel Citadel's indestructible as unclassified; the goldfish reads interaction in hand 79.5% on turn 6 but castable only 19.3% of the time that turn, the gap being mana spent on the board. The deck has no way to regrow Sai, so this stage protects the artifacts and leaves the commander to the tax.

evidence.note: six of the eight sit together in city-1 (Counterspell, Negate, Launch Mishap, Aetherize, Propaganda, Signpost); Padeem is in city-3 and Shimmer Myr in city-4

stages.label: ONE BODY THAT IS THE WHOLE BOARD
stages.what_it_does: How the game ends: a body whose size is the artifact count, or one that brings its own army. Darksteel Juggernaut (indestructible, power equal to artifacts, must attack) and Broodstar (affinity, flying, power equal to artifacts) are the board in one creature; Myr Battlesphere brings four Myr and taps X Myr on attack for +X/+0 and X damage to the defending player — Silver Myr, Palladium Myr, Myr Retriever and Shimmer Myr are Myr too; Graaz makes every other creature a 5/3 Juggernaut, so a Thopter swarm becomes 5-power flyers; Kappa Cannoneer grows and goes unblockable whenever it or another artifact you control enters, improvises off the board, and has ward {4}; Steel Hellkite flies, pumps for {2} and wipes a mana value off any player it hits. The goldfish reads the declared KILL group (eight bodies AND one of Chief, Master, Overseer, Nettlecyst, Omnitool, Rogue) assembled by turn 6 in 43.4% of games, 67.4% ever, mean turn 4.862; its six-card connector half is the thinnest component in the deck at 36.4% of openers. Combat without the Thopters: median kill turn 10, mean 9.508, 48.9% of games with no kill by turn 10, kill by turn 8 in 4.0% and by turn 9 in 21.0%; mean damage 11.498 by turn 10. These are floors — Sai's tokens are not in them — and the model has no blockers. Whether the kill is the wide board or the one body is the open question CONTEXT.md names; this model says the two are usually the same card: Juggernaut and Broodstar are sized by the artifact count, Battlesphere and Kappa by the bodies that enter, Graaz sizes the swarm instead of itself, and Steel Hellkite is the one fixed body.

evidence.note: Juggernaut, Broodstar and Hellkite in city-4; Battlesphere and Graaz in city-0; Kappa in city-3

three cards carry it (Graaz, Kappa, Rogue); Juggernaut is protection:self + threat:body, Broodstar ramp:cost-reduction + threat:body, Battlesphere threat:body + threat:tokens + value:etb, Hellkite buff:pump + removal:sweeper + threat:body — none of those four is tagged wincon:combat

lines.note: Stack 001 (checker pass): Chief of the Foundry cast with Sai and Master of Etherium on the board — Sai's trigger resolves first, the Thopter enters before Chief, and once the stack is empty Sai is 1/4, the Thopter 3/3, Master of Etherium 4/4 and Chief 3/4. One artifact cast added two artifacts and Master grew by three (two bodies plus Chief's anthem).
CLAIM: one artifact cast is one Thopter and one card — Sai's trigger and Archmage's trigger fire on the same event. Needs a stack.
CLAIM: the upkeep Thopter is a body with no cast (it needs an artifact already on the board — 'if you control an artifact'), and two of them are a card through Sai's {1}{U} sacrifice. Needs a stack.
CLAIM: Retriever dying to Sai's sacrifice returns Wellspring to hand; re-cast for {1} under Sculptor it draws again and makes another Thopter. Needs a stack.
CLAIM: tap two Thopters, Juggernaut cannot be blocked at power equal to the artifact count. Needs a stack: can Thopters made this turn pay Rogue's tap-two cost?

Stack 002 (checker pass): with Sai, Rogue and Battlesphere on the board, Rogue's 'tap two untapped artifacts you control' is legally paid by two Thopters created this turn — 302.6 restricts only a creature's own {T} abilities — and Myr Battlesphere cannot be blocked this combat; the tapped Thopters cannot pay a second activation that turn.
CLAIM: Overseer's counter lands on Battlesphere and all four Myr; the attack then taps the Myr for +X and X damage. Needs a stack on the ordering of the tap-for-mana and tap-for-Battlesphere choices.
CLAIM: the two mana Myr are Myr for Battlesphere's attack trigger, so an untapped mana Myr is +1 damage instead of one mana. Needs a stack.
CLAIM: {U} and bounce a Thopter token puts Battlesphere onto the battlefield from hand; its ETB makes four Myr but Sai makes no Thopter because nothing was cast. Needs a stack.

CLAIM: Monument's 'whenever you tap a permanent for {C}, add an additional {C}' makes Sol Ring THREE, not four — one trigger per tap event, and the 2020-09-25 ruling (an input, not a citation) says a tap for more than one {C} adds only one. Needs a stack on 605.1a / 603.2 to restate it as a fact.
CLAIM: Shimmer Myr lets the artifacts be cast on an opponent's end step, so Sai's Thopters arrive after a sorcery-speed wrath. Needs a stack.

CLAIM: Thoughtcast's two draws are two life from each opponent with Crawler out. Needs a stack. The goldfish cannot size this line: Thoughtcast is in meta.card_advantage.draw_not_modelled, so its draws are absent from the 2.92 cumulative event damage by turn 10, which reads only Scrawling Crawler's upkeep draws and the modelled draws that reach Psychosis Crawler.

map_disagreements.why: Master of Etherium ('power equal to the number of artifacts you control') sits in city-3 THE ENGINE ROOM beside Sai; Nettlecyst, Adaptive Omnitool and the two count-sized bodies sit together in city-4's hood SIZED BY THE COUNT; Chief of the Foundry ('other artifact creatures get +1/+1'), Steel Overseer and Forsaken Monument sit in city-0 THE COLOURLESS CORE. The map did see the count-sizing — its hood is named for it — but it split the scalers on whether the text also names Sai's trigger-shaped job (Master, Rogue, Transmuter) or a flat anthem (Chief, Monument). What makes all nine one stage is what they do TO the Thopters.

Broodstar and Darksteel Juggernaut are in city-4's hood SIZED BY THE COUNT ('threats whose power is the number of artifacts you control'), which is the right reading; Steel Hellkite is in the other hood THE BIG FLIERS ('evasive finishers with a fixed size'); Battlesphere and Graaz are in city-0 on their token and Juggernaut text; Kappa in city-3 on 'improvise'. The narrow disagreement is that Master of Etherium, which shares the count-sizing text, sits in city-3 beside Sai rather than with the two bodies, and that the kill stage spans three cities because the map clusters each body on its own keywords where the engine groups them on what the board does to them.

Ichor Wellspring says 'draw', Myr Retriever says 'return', Thopter Spy Network and Thopter Fabricator say 'create a Thopter'. None says 'sacrifice'; the sacrifice outlet is on the commander, who is not in the 99 the map clusters. This is the stage least visible in card text and the one the goldfish does not model either.

map_disagreements.component: fuel — the draw suite and the two discounts
map_disagreements.why: The affinity cantrips and Sculptor cluster beside Sai in THE ENGINE ROOM on the word 'artifact'; Research Thief, Pull from Tomorrow and the Logbook cluster with the counterspells in THE MOAT (fallback name 'Mana') on instant-speed blue text; the Tome and Mind's Eye with the colourless artifacts in THE COLOURLESS CORE. The map's fallback names ('Mana' for the counterspell city, 'Card Flow' for the rock city THE MANA THAT COUNTS) are a measurement and this model does not rename them.

map_disagreements.component: the declared KILL and PAYOFF groups
map_disagreements.why: engine-facts: 0 of 6 declared components sit in a single city. The declaration groups by what a card does to the board; the map groups by what a card says.

open_questions.question: Master Transmuter activates returning a Thopter token to hand and puts Myr Battlesphere onto the battlefield: does Sai trigger (expected no — not cast), do Kappa Cannoneer's 'another artifact enters' and Battlesphere's four-Myr ETB fire, and does the token simply cease to exist?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Transmuter is in the declared KILL body group; the pilot needs to know the cheat-in costs a Thopter and earns none, and how many Kappa counters it yields.

open_questions.question: Myr Battlesphere attacks with Silver Myr and Palladium Myr untapped and Steel Overseer on board: in what order are the Overseer activation, the mana taps and the Battlesphere X-tap chosen, and what is the damage to the defending player?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Two of the deck's mana sources are Myr; the mana→wincon line claims each is +1 damage instead of one mana, and the ordering decides whether the pilot can have both.

open_questions.question: All Is Dust resolves with the deck's typical board: which of the 18 coloured nonland permanents in the 99 plus Sai from the command zone (Master of Etherium, Etherium Sculptor, Kappa Cannoneer, Master Transmuter, Padeem, Shimmer Dragon, Whirler Rogue among them) are sacrificed, and do colourless Thopter tokens and Nettlecyst's black Germ stay or go?
open_questions.why_it_matters: All Is Dust is one of two sweepers and it eats the commander and most of the conversion stage while sparing the tokens; the Germ is black and goes.

open_questions.question: Kappa Cannoneer cast with improvise, tapping Thopters: does Sai's trigger resolve first so the new Thopter enters before Kappa, meaning Kappa does NOT get a counter from it, and does Kappa's own entry give it its first counter?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Kappa is in the KILL group and self-connects; its size on the turn it lands decides whether it attacks unblockably that turn or the next.

open_questions.question: Model Sai's cast trigger (a 1/1 flying artifact token per artifact spell cast) and his {1}{U} sacrifice-two draw: what do mean bodies by turn 6 (floor 2.567), the KILL group's by-turn-6 rate (floor 43.4%) and median kill turn (floor 10) read with the commander's abilities on?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every board and damage figure in this model is a floor because the Thopters are not modelled; the pilot cannot size the swarm from the current artifact.

open_questions.question: Forsaken Monument on the battlefield, tap Sol Ring for {C}{C}: does Monument's 'whenever you tap a permanent for {C}' trigger once and add one {C} (three total) or add one per {C} produced (four)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The mana→conversion line and the mana stage both state three; the 2020-09-25 ruling says one additional {C} per tap, and the model wants that as a cited fact rather than a ruling read as one.

open_questions.question: For a mono-blue artifact go-wide deck at bracket 2, does the archetype close with the anthem-scaled swarm or with the single self-sized body, and what does the table typically do to it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: CONTEXT.md names 'wide board or one big body' as the deck's open question; this model says the two are usually the same card, which a strategy frame can confirm or refute before the first logged game.

findings.claim: Monument's 'whenever you tap a permanent for {C}, add an additional {C}' makes Sol Ring four
findings.note: The quoted text says 'an additional {C}' per trigger and the trigger is one tap event. WotC ruling 2020-09-25 (card-rulings, an input not a citation): 'If you tap a permanent for more than one {C}, you add only one additional {C}.' Sol Ring under Monument is three. The line is dashed, but a dashed line whose claim is wrong is still wrong, and the stage text repeats it as 'doubled'. Settle it with a stack (CR 605.1a mana abilities / 603.2 trigger events) and restate as three.
